none.workflow:
There is no backlog and no PR integration here, so the work arrives in the conversation and the local repository is the only context.

- A described feature, bug or refactor: clarify if needed, then `pc-plan-propose` when the change is worth planning, or straight to `pc-plan-apply`.
- An existing OpenSpec change, plus any of `implement` / `start` / `go`: `pc-plan-apply`.
- `just do it` or `quick fix`: work in this session, no proposal, no ceremony.

A GitHub or Azure DevOps URL is not a trigger in this mode; re-run onboarding to configure a platform.
none.skillsGuide: No platform skills installed (platform: none). Work from direct user instructions and local OpenSpec artifacts only.

azure.workflow:
An Azure DevOps work item or PR URL in the user's message means run the pipeline, in whatever words it arrives, unless they asked for analysis or context only.

- Work item URL: `pc-userstory` to parse it, `pc-plan-propose` for the plan, confirm, `pc-plan-apply` to build, then ship.
- An existing OpenSpec change, plus any of `implement` / `start` / `go`: `pc-plan-apply`, then ship.
- A PR URL with a feedback or fix request: read the PR comments, fix, update the PR.
azure.skillsGuide:
Platform skills (Azure DevOps):
- `@pc-userstory`: load when an Azure DevOps work item URL is detected. Fetches the work item via `az` CLI and creates an OpenSpec change. NEVER use browser tools for Azure DevOps operations.
- `pc-ops-ship`: load in ship mode to create a PR and link the work item, or in feedback mode to read and classify PR review comments.

github.workflow:
A GitHub Issue or PR URL in the user's message means run the pipeline, in whatever words it arrives, unless they asked for analysis or context only.

- Issue URL: `pc-userstory` to parse it, `pc-plan-propose` for the plan, confirm, `pc-plan-apply` to build, then ship.
- An existing OpenSpec change, plus any of `implement` / `start` / `go`: `pc-plan-apply`, then ship.
- A PR URL with a feedback or fix request: read the PR comments, fix, update the PR.
github.skillsGuide:
Platform skills (GitHub):
- `@pc-userstory`: load when a GitHub Issue URL is detected. Fetches the issue via `gh` CLI and creates an OpenSpec change. NEVER use webfetch to access GitHub URLs.
- `pc-ops-ship`: load in ship mode to create a PR with screenshots, or in feedback mode to read and classify PR review comments.

default.workflow:
The backlog and the repo are on different platforms here: `.opencode/harness.json` → `platform.backlog` and `platform.repo`. Never cross them. Work items always come from the backlog CLI and pull requests always from the repo CLI, or the command fails against the wrong host and the fallback is a page fetch that is denied.

A work item URL, or a PR URL with a feedback request, means run the pipeline, in whatever words it arrives, unless the user asked for analysis or context only.

- Work item URL or issue key: `pc-userstory` (backlog CLI) to parse it, `pc-plan-propose` for the plan, confirm, `pc-plan-apply` to build, `pc-ops-ship` (repo CLI) to ship.
- An existing OpenSpec change, plus any of `implement` / `start` / `go`: `pc-plan-apply`, then ship.
- A PR or MR URL with a feedback or fix request: read its comments through the repo CLI, fix, update it.
default.skillsGuide:
Mixed platform setup: the two platform skills target different hosts:
- `@pc-userstory` → fetches work items from the backlog platform. Load when a work-item URL or issue key is provided.
- `pc-ops-ship` → creates PRs/MRs and triages review feedback on the repo platform. Load in ship mode or PR-feedback mode.

jira.workflow:
A Jira URL or a bare issue key (`PROJ-123`) means run the pipeline, in whatever words it arrives, unless they asked for analysis or context only.

- Either one: `pc-userstory` to fetch it through `acli jira`, `pc-plan-propose` for the plan, confirm, `pc-plan-apply` to build, then ship.
- An existing OpenSpec change, plus any of `implement` / `start` / `go`: `pc-plan-apply`, then ship.

Jira has no pull requests: PR work runs on the repo platform in `platform.repo`.
jira.skillsGuide:
### Backlog Platform: Jira
- `pc-userstory` -> fetches Jira work items via `acli jira` CLI. Load when a Jira URL or issue key is provided.

### Repo Platform
- PR skills are loaded based on `platform.repo` (GitHub or Azure DevOps).

gitlab.workflow:
A backlog work item URL, or a GitLab MR URL with a feedback request, means run the pipeline, in whatever words it arrives, unless they asked for analysis or context only.

- Work item URL: `pc-userstory` to fetch it through the backlog CLI, `pc-plan-propose` for the plan, confirm, `pc-plan-apply` to build, then ship.
- An existing OpenSpec change, plus any of `implement` / `start` / `go`: `pc-plan-apply`, then ship.
- An MR URL with a feedback or fix request: `glab mr note list`, triage, fix, update the MR.

GitLab has no backlog here: work items come from the platform in `platform.backlog`.
gitlab.skillsGuide:
### Repo Platform: GitLab
- `pc-ops-ship` -> creates GitLab merge requests via `glab` CLI. Load when shipping a branch or processing MR feedback.

### Backlog Platform
- Work item skills are loaded based on `platform.backlog` (GitHub / Azure / Jira).

browser.workflow:
Any work item URL means run the pipeline, whichever tool it points at, unless the user asked for analysis or context only.

- The URL: `pc-userstory` to open and read the page, `pc-plan-propose` for the plan, confirm, `pc-plan-apply` to build, then ship.
- An existing OpenSpec change, plus any of `implement` / `start` / `go`: `pc-plan-apply`, then ship.

Browser is backlog-only: PR work runs on the repo platform in `platform.repo`.
browser.skillsGuide:
### Backlog Platform: Others (Browser)
- `pc-userstory` -> opens work item URLs via agent-browser, reads page content, creates OpenSpec changes. Load when a URL the user provides does not match GitHub/Azure/Jira CLI platforms.

### Repo Platform
- PR skills are loaded based on `platform.repo` (GitHub / Azure DevOps / GitLab).
